      "title": "Strategy close shuts down the factory-shared FixedQueuePool",
      "body": "ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ (result_consumer.py line 133) and reuses it for every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate/join shuts that pool down, stopping worker threads and closing the queues. Arroyo closes the old strategy on partition revocation/reassignment, so after a rebalance the factory will create new strategies around an already shut-down pool. New messages then cannot be processed, and enqueue attempts may fail or be dropped. The pool lifecycle must match the strategy lifecycle, or the pool must be recreated on each assignment."

      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Unbounded worker queues provide no backpressure",
      "body": "Each worker queue is created as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and FixedQueuePool.submit puts items unconditionally. If workers are slower than the consumer—exactly the slow-item case this PR is trying to address—the consumer will keep polling and enqueuing full Kafka payloads without bound. poll() only emits a gauge and does not block or raise. This can cause unbounded memory growth. Use bounded queues, block in submit, or apply backpressure in poll."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Offsets are completed and can be committed even when processing fails",
      "body": "OrderedQueueWorker.run marks the offset complete in finally, so an exception from result_processor still allows the offset to become committable. ResultProcessor.__call__ in result_consumer.py also swallows all exceptions and only logs them. The result is that failed results can be committed and never retried, contradicting the strategy docstring claim that offsets are committed only after successful processing. This can silently drop uptime results. Failures should prevent completion, or be routed to retry/DLQ."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 317,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "submit() marks offsets complete when it cannot enqueue/process a message",
      "body": "SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, if the message has a BrokerValue, immediately adds and completes the offset. This includes decoder/grouping errors and failures from queue_pool.submit, such as submitting to a shut-down queue. The message is not processed, but its offset becomes committable. That turns transient or operational errors into silent data loss. Errors should be surfaced, retried, dead-lettered, or should block the consumer rather than completing the offset."
    },

      "title": "OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets while other threads mutate it",
      "body": "OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets iterates list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock, while add_offset can concurrently insert new partition keys from the consumer thread. Concurrent mutation of the partition dictionary can cause RuntimeError during iteration or inconsistent snapshots. Protect the partition set with a global lock, or copy/modify it under a lock."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 233,
      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Shutdown stops workers before draining queues and join ignores its timeout",
      "body": "FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues, so each worker exits after finishing its current item instead of draining remaining queued work. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) calls close() and ignores the timeout, forcibly shutting down the pool. Queued items are dropped on shutdown/rebalance instead of being processed up to the requested timeout. It should wait_until_empty(timeout) and only stop workers after draining or after the timeout expires."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py",
      "line": 132,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",

      "body": "OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown, and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). These APIs were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older supported Python version, shutdown will not work correctly: Queue.shutdown will raise AttributeError (caught and logged), workers may never be woken from queue.get(), and exception handling can fail. Add a fallback for older Python versions or explicitly enforce Python 3.13+."
    },

      "body": "SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy's decoder type accepts KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload, but ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload begins with assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload). Any FilteredPayload message therefore raises AssertionError, which SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit treats as a generic submission error and logs. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly by returning None so they can be skipped without exception/log spam."
    },

With unbounded queues, this unnecessarily retains full Kafka payloads in memory. Remove the unused message field or store only the required metadata."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py",
      "line": 136,

A negative num_queues creates no queues and later hash(group_key) % num_queues or queue lookup can fail. Validate that max_workers/num_queues is a positive integer when using thread-queue-parallel."

findings.title: Strategy close shuts down the factory-shared FixedQueuePool
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ (result_consumer.py line 133) and reuses it for every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate/join shuts that pool down, stopping worker threads and closing the queues. Arroyo closes the old strategy on partition revocation/reassignment, so after a rebalance the factory will create new strategies around an already shut-down pool. New messages then cannot be processed, and enqueue attempts may fail or be dropped. The pool lifecycle must match the strategy lifecycle, or the pool must be recreated on each assignment.

findings.title: Unbounded worker queues provide no backpressure
findings.body: Each worker queue is created as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and FixedQueuePool.submit puts items unconditionally. If workers are slower than the consumer—exactly the slow-item case this PR is trying to address—the consumer will keep polling and enqueuing full Kafka payloads without bound. poll() only emits a gauge and does not block or raise. This can cause unbounded memory growth. Use bounded queues, block in submit, or apply backpressure in poll.

findings.title: Offsets are completed and can be committed even when processing fails
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run marks the offset complete in finally, so an exception from result_processor still allows the offset to become committable. ResultProcessor.__call__ in result_consumer.py also swallows all exceptions and only logs them. The result is that failed results can be committed and never retried, contradicting the strategy docstring claim that offsets are committed only after successful processing. This can silently drop uptime results. Failures should prevent completion, or be routed to retry/DLQ.

findings.title: submit() marks offsets complete when it cannot enqueue/process a message
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, if the message has a BrokerValue, immediately adds and completes the offset. This includes decoder/grouping errors and failures from queue_pool.submit, such as submitting to a shut-down queue. The message is not processed, but its offset becomes committable. That turns transient or operational errors into silent data loss. Errors should be surfaced, retried, dead-lettered, or should block the consumer rather than completing the offset.

findings.title: OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets while other threads mutate it
findings.body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets iterates list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock, while add_offset can concurrently insert new partition keys from the consumer thread. Concurrent mutation of the partition dictionary can cause RuntimeError during iteration or inconsistent snapshots. Protect the partition set with a global lock, or copy/modify it under a lock.

findings.title: Shutdown stops workers before draining queues and join ignores its timeout
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues, so each worker exits after finishing its current item instead of draining remaining queued work. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) calls close() and ignores the timeout, forcibly shutting down the pool. Queued items are dropped on shutdown/rebalance instead of being processed up to the requested timeout. It should wait_until_empty(timeout) and only stop workers after draining or after the timeout expires.

findings.title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue.ShutDown/Queue.shutdown APIs
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown, and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). These APIs were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older supported Python version, shutdown will not work correctly: Queue.shutdown will raise AttributeError (caught and logged), workers may never be woken from queue.get(), and exception handling can fail. Add a fallback for older Python versions or explicitly enforce Python 3.13+.

findings.title: decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload instead of handling it
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy's decoder type accepts KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload, but ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload begins with assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload). Any FilteredPayload message therefore raises AssertionError, which SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit treats as a generic submission error and logs. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly by returning None so they can be skipped without exception/log spam.

findings.title: WorkItem retains the full Kafka message though it is unused
findings.body: WorkItem stores the original Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], but only partition and offset are used for offset tracking; the message field is never read. With unbounded queues, this unnecessarily retains full Kafka payloads in memory. Remove the unused message field or store only the required metadata.

findings.title: max_workers is not validated for thread-queue-parallel mode
findings.body: FixedQueuePool is created with num_queues=max_workers or 20. This treats 0 as 20, but negative values are passed through. A negative num_queues creates no queues and later hash(group_key) % num_queues or queue lookup can fail. Validate that max_workers/num_queues is a positive integer when using thread-queue-parallel.
